articles.title: Comparative outcomes of Bernese periacetabular osteotomy in adolescents, young adults, and middle-aged adults : a minimum two-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Chen YH, Lee CC, Wu KW, Chen YH, Yao SH, Lee TL, et al.
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic hip dysplasia undergoing Bernese periacetabular osteotomy, stratified by age: adolescents (11-19 years), young adults (20-39 years), and middle-aged adults (40-57 years)
articles.sample_size: 68 patients (68 hips): 16 adolescents, 18 young adults, 14 middle-aged adults
articles.outcomes: Radiological parameters, complication rates, pain scores (VAS), modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), and osteotomy union times
articles.take_home: Middle-aged patients selected for hip dysplasia surgery showed similar improvements in pain and function to younger patients at two-year follow-up, though their bones took longer to heal (13 months versus 6 months). The longer healing time did not negatively affect their final results or recovery.

articles.title: Immunogenicity of fractional one-fifth and one-half doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine compared with full dose in children aged 9-23 months in Uganda: a phase 4, single-blind, randomised clinical trial.
articles.authors: Doshi RH, Lubega I, Muhoza P, Carlock G, Sekiziyivu AB, Tuttle A, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 9-23 months in Kampala, Uganda with no previous yellow fever disease or vaccination
articles.sample_size: 1784 participants (600 one-fifth dose, 594 one-half dose, 590 full dose)
articles.outcomes: Seroconversion (antibody response) at 4 weeks, 1 year, and 13-48 months measured by plaque reduction neutralisation test
articles.take_home: Both smaller fractional doses of yellow fever vaccine (one-fifth and one-half) were just as effective as the standard full dose at triggering an immune response in young children. These results suggest fractional doses could be used when vaccine supplies are limited during outbreaks.

articles.title: Management and Outcome of Kirschner Wire-related Osteomyelitis in Pediatric Patients After Treatment of Closed Fracture.
articles.authors: Lao J, Bai H, Lu S, Li G, Ali S, Zhu T, et al.
articles.population: Children with acute or chronic osteomyelitis after Kirschner wire fixation for closed fractures
articles.sample_size: 16 patients (11 male, 5 female; average age 7.4 years)
articles.outcomes: Healing without recurrence in all patients; joint function and normal daily life maintained; complications included septic arthritis (73%), secondary ossification centre necrosis (60%) and premature growth plate closure (60%)
articles.take_home: Kirschner wire fixation can occasionally lead to bone infection along the wire path, sometimes affecting joints and growth plates. Early surgical cleaning and antibiotic-impregnated bone grafts successfully healed all infections, with patients maintaining good joint function and normal activities despite some bone complications.

articles.title: One in Four Children Experience BMI Increase After Lower Extremity Surgery Without Return to Preoperative Levels: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Viza Gomes P, Badejo M, Damron A, Bradley T, Bitolas R, Sachs B, et al.
articles.population: Children under 18 years undergoing operative treatment for lower extremity fractures or elective lower extremity surgery
articles.outcomes: Change in BMI from baseline to 3 months postoperatively and return to preoperative BMI levels by 12-18 months
articles.take_home: Around one in four children experienced a clinically meaningful increase in BMI within 3 months of lower extremity surgery, and most of these children had not returned to their preoperative BMI by 12-18 months. Children treated for obesity-related conditions were at higher risk of BMI increase than those treated for fractures.

articles.title: Can you FORCE research implementation? A PERUKI survey to evaluate knowledge translation of the FORCE study.
articles.authors: Jenkins M, Bennett JF, Roland D, Perry DC
articles.population: Paediatric Emergency Department clinicians in the UK and Ireland
articles.outcomes: Uptake of FORCE trial findings into clinical practice for managing torus fractures in children; awareness of trial; use of dissemination tools; barriers and enablers to implementation
articles.take_home: Most clinicians became aware of the FORCE trial and changed their practice to use soft bandages or no immobilization for torus fractures, but dissemination tools and peer influence were crucial - simply publishing results was not enough to ensure change happened consistently.

articles.title: Publication Volume and Fellowship Characteristics Are Associated With Future Academic Faculty Appointments in Pediatric Orthopaedic Surgery.
articles.authors: Silvestre J, Kodali P, Hosseinzadeh P, Sankar WN, Flynn JM
articles.population: Pediatric orthopaedic surgery fellows from 2017 to 2023
articles.sample_size: 473 fellows (284 in academic positions, 189 in non-academic positions)
articles.outcomes: Factors associated with obtaining future academic faculty appointments, including publication volume, medical school type, additional degrees, and fellowship program size
articles.take_home: Fellows who published more research papers before their fellowship, graduated from larger fellowship programmes, and had additional graduate-level degrees were more likely to become academic faculty. The top three fellowship programmes produced 29% of all future academic appointments, suggesting that training location matters significantly for career outcomes.

articles.title: Use of the bacterial lysate OM-85 for the primary prevention of wheezing lower respiratory illness in preschool children: a randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
articles.authors: Morgan WJ, Mauger DT, Bacharier LB, Bauer CS, Davis SD, Fitzpatrick AM, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 6-18 months at increased risk for asthma due to atopic dermatitis, parental asthma, or asthma in a sibling
articles.sample_size: 822 children randomly assigned (411 to OM-85, 411 to placebo)
articles.outcomes: Time to first wheezing lower respiratory tract illness during 36-month observation period off study drug
articles.take_home: OM-85 bacterial lysate did not reduce wheezing illness in young children at high risk of asthma compared to placebo. Bacterial lysates are not effective for preventing asthma-like symptoms in preschool children.

articles.title: Wealth redistribution policies to mitigate the impact of development assistance defunding: a retrospective evaluation and forecasting analysis up to 2030.
articles.authors: Sibils GB, Anderle RVR, da Silva AF, de Sales LOF, Pena D, Monti C, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective impact evaluation and forecasting analysis
articles.outcomes: All-cause mortality, under-5 mortality, and projected averted deaths under ten wealth redistribution policy scenarios by 2030
articles.take_home: Higher development assistance funding was associated with significant reductions in mortality rates. Wealth redistribution policies such as taxes on ultra-high-net-worth individuals could avert millions of deaths by 2030 if implemented to replace current aid funding cuts.

articles.title: The Duration of Pavlik Harness Wear Following Successful Reduction of Dislocated Hips Does Not Play a Role in Determining Radiographic Dysplasia at 2 Years.
articles.authors: Sinha R, Siebert M, Worrall H, Jo CH, Morris WZ, Kim H, et al.
articles.population: Newborns with developmental dysplasia of the hip (dislocated hips) treated with Pavlik harness
articles.outcomes: Residual acetabular dysplasia at 2-year follow-up, measured by acetabular index
articles.take_home: How long a baby wears a Pavlik harness for a dislocated hip does not affect whether the hip socket develops normally by age 2. About 12 weeks of harness wear was associated with a low rate of ongoing problems.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of management of primary medial epicondylar fractures: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Bonczar M, Ostrowski P, Wilk J, Jastrzebski I, Walocha J, Koziej M, et al.
articles.population: Children and adults with primary medial epicondyle fractures
articles.outcomes: Fracture union rate, complication rate, functional outcomes
articles.take_home: Surgery achieves much higher healing rates (97%) compared to conservative treatment (46%), with lower overall complications from surgery (21%) than immobilisation alone (36%). Screw fixation was the most reliable surgical option.
